rationale: Client construction and certificate requests dominate, but the substantial bootstrap/context/truststore section spills into adjacent configuration and operational topics without explicit delegation. Most mechanics have line-range citations, but central claims about universal CaClient adoption and intended cross-command sharedContext hand-offs lack evidence establishing those conclusions. The page describes flows and restrictions without two developed causal explanations; global-state isolation, concurrency, and partial-bootstrap failure consequences remain unexplained. Change guides provide concrete locations and ordered edits, but no named tests or validation/failure checks. The API-extension advice is materially misleading: a ClientOption or external helper cannot make *ca.Client satisfy an added interface method. Organization makes the main paths easy to find, but edge cases are scattered rather than presented as a separate progressive-disclosure layer.

The page explicitly owns certificate-group tooling and delegates online CA issuance to the adjacent CA topic. Most command mechanics have precise line-range citations, but the central assertion that everything runs locally or against a TLS endpoint lacks sufficient evidence; template-engine capabilities and root-package registration also lack exact supporting evidence. The page catalogs flows and restrictions without two developed causal explanations connecting implementation choices to consequences. Change guides provide concrete locations and ordered edits, but no explicit validation procedure or named tests for those changes. Organization is readable and failure handling is grouped, though the main body remains a flat command reference rather than progressive disclosure. The opening's categorical local-or-TLS characterization conflicts with its later description of AIA retrieval and OCSP/CRL network requests, whose transport is not established as TLS-only.

The CA command group clearly dominates, but substantial renewal-daemon and provisioner details overlap adjacent outline topics without explicit delegation or exclusions. Most major descriptions have line-range citations, yet some command-purpose claims have only file locators, and claims such as each name action supporting --remove exceed the evidence explained on the page. The page describes useful flows, authentication selection, scheduling, and policy initialization, but largely lists mechanics rather than developing causal invariants or failure consequences. Concrete implementation locations are plentiful, but there is no ordered change procedure or named validation check. Headings make this a readable flat reference; edge cases remain mixed into operational descriptions rather than forming a progressive-disclosure layer. No material contradiction is apparent from the supplied page, though its evidence does not establish exhaustive correctness.

Distribution and operational integration dominate, but the substantial integration-test survey belongs to Build, Test, and Change Guides, and the page states no exclusions or delegation boundaries. All source references are paths or symbols without line ranges or quoted excerpts, so none qualifies as specific evidence for load-bearing claims. The page describes packaging, renewal, and server lifecycle mechanics with a few implications, but does not develop two substantial causal explanations into an invariant or failure model. Concrete files and named failure tests support basic change navigation; an ordered edit sequence and rollback/debugging guidance are absent. The opening and headings make this a readable flat reference, but operational edge cases are not separately developed. No material contradiction is established by the supplied page; its explicit infrastructure uncertainty is useful, but unsupported technical details prevent stronger confidence.
